Depends on your audience. I think they're more popular with casual gamers, and you'd have a tough time marketing a hidden object game to anyone who isn't strictly a casual gamer.

I enjoy them. I got into them while I was working a customer service job where I had a lot of downtime (often around 5-10 minutes). I couldn't play other games, and I could just stop when I needed to help a customer. Now I play them as a way to help me fall asleep. It keeps my mind occupied, but not so much that I have to really concentrate. If I wasn't saving all of them to play for this purpose, I would probably play some during my free time. I've recently been playing Artifex Mundi ones, they're a mixture of Hidden object and point and click adventure games. Great quality.

All in all, it's a relatively niche market, but popular in its own way. Most players are strictly casual gamers, and I believe they're often marketed towards women.
I prefer a more interactive experience in my games, but I'm sure you'd have an audience with younger people and people who don't play video games "seriously".
